subject: social_science

concepts.title: Military Coup
concepts.definition: A sudden, illegal seizure of power from a government, often carried out by military forces.
concepts.key_idea: Illegal transition of power from elected leaders to military control.
question_patterns: define a military coup
how does a military coup affect democracy
what happened in Chile in 1973
identify the features of a coup
why is a coup considered undemocratic

solution_steps.explain: A coup involves the removal of an elected government by force.

concepts.title: Democratic Transition
concepts.definition: The process by which a country moves from an authoritarian or non-democratic regime to a democratic system.
concepts.key_idea: Shift from dictatorship to elected governance through public mandate.
question_patterns: describe the transition to democracy in Poland
how was democracy restored in Chile
what role do elections play in democratic transition
explain the shift from army rule to democracy
why is transition a complex process

solution_steps.explain: Transition involves ending autocratic control and establishing civil rights.

concepts.title: Universal Adult Franchise
concepts.definition: The right of every adult citizen to vote in elections, regardless of their wealth, gender, or social status.
concepts.key_idea: Political equality through equal voting rights for all adults.
question_patterns: what is universal adult franchise
why is universal suffrage important
when was universal franchise granted in India
how does franchise promote democracy
explain the principle of one person one vote

solution_steps.explain: Every adult gets a single vote of equal weight.

concepts.title: Global Institutional Democracy
concepts.definition: The extent to which international organizations allow member countries to have an equal say in decision-making.
concepts.key_idea: Evaluating if international bodies like the UN or IMF treat all nations equally.
question_patterns: are global institutions democratic
how does the UN security council function
why is the IMF criticized for lack of democracy
what is veto power in the UN
how can global democracy be strengthened

solution_steps.explain: Compare equal voting vs weighted voting in global bodies.

concepts.title: Representative Democracy
concepts.definition: A governance model where the populace selects delegates to exercise power and manage public affairs on their behalf.
concepts.key_idea: Indirect rule necessitated by large populations and practical constraints.
question_patterns: What is the most common form of democracy today?
Why is direct rule by all citizens impossible in modern states?
Explain the concept of representative democracy.
How do majorities exercise power in a modern democracy?
Why can't all citizens sit together to take collective decisions?

solution_steps.action: Identify the scale of the population
solution_steps.explain: Modern nations have millions of citizens, making physical assembly impossible.
Individual citizens often lack the time, expertise, or interest to decide on every policy.
Power is delegated to elected officials who act as intermediaries for the majority.

concepts.title: Democratic Decision Making
concepts.definition: A process involving discussion and agreement from everyone impacted by a choice, ensuring equal influence for all members.
concepts.key_idea: Consultation and consent across all spheres of life, from families to governments.
question_patterns: What does a democratic decision involve?
How can the principle of democracy be applied to a family?
What is the basic principle of taking decisions democratically?
Does democracy only apply to the government?
Explain the role of consultation in democratic processes.

solution_steps.explain: Determine all individuals who will be affected by the specific decision.
Grant those with less power the same weight in discussion as those with more power.
Engage in consultation until a collective agreement or consent is achieved.

concepts.title: Ideal Democracy Standards
concepts.definition: A benchmark for governance that requires total equality in resources, information, and participation for every citizen.
concepts.key_idea: A goal to strive for that helps identify the weaknesses of existing systems.
question_patterns: What is meant by an ideal democracy?
How does the ideal of democracy help us judge existing governments?
What are the requirements for equal role in decision making?
Why is no country in the world a perfect democracy?
Distinguish between a minimal democracy and a good democracy.

solution_steps.explain: Institutional features like voting rights constitute a minimal democracy.
Assess if citizens have equal education, health, and information.
Use the ideal standard to identify gaps in the current democratic setup.

concepts.title: Direct Democracy and Gram Sabha
concepts.definition: A system where all members of a small community participate directly in the decision-making process without representatives.
concepts.key_idea: Direct participation is feasible and necessary in small local communities.
question_patterns: How should a Gram Sabha work in a village?
In what situation can people take decisions directly?
Is direct democracy possible in a small community?
Give an example of direct democratic decision making in India.
Contrast Gram Sabha with parliamentary democracy.

solution_steps.explain: Ensure the community is small enough for everyone to meet.
All eligible members sit together in a common forum.
Decisions are made by the assembly rather than elected delegates.

concepts.title: Political Participation Rate
concepts.definition: The percentage of a specific demographic group that exercises their right to vote in an election.
concepts.key_idea: Participation levels often correlate with socio-economic status.
question_patterns: Calculate the voting percentage of a group.
What is the participation rate if 5 out of 10 people vote?
Find the percentage of voters in the top income bracket.
How much is the participation rate for the bottom 20 percent?
Compare the voting rates of two different income groups.

solution_steps.explain: voters is the count of people who cast a ballot
total_group is the size of the sample or demographic
Divide voters by total and multiply by 100

concepts.title: Income Inequality Ratio
concepts.definition: A numerical comparison showing the disparity in wealth or earnings between two different social groups.
concepts.key_idea: Economic gaps can translate into unequal political influence.
question_patterns: What is the income ratio between the two families?
How many times more wealth does the rich group have compared to the poor?
Calculate the disparity ratio of income.
Find the wealth multiplier between group A and group B.
Compare the average earnings of two demographics.

solution_steps.explain: income_high is the larger value in the comparison
income_low is the smaller value in the comparison
Divide the higher value by the lower value

concepts.title: Active Political Participation
concepts.definition: The requirement in a democracy for citizens to engage in political activities to ensure the health of the system.
concepts.key_idea: The fate of a democracy depends on the actions of its citizens, not just its rulers.
question_patterns: Why does democracy depend on active political participation?
How do citizens make a difference to a country's democracy?
What distinguishes democracy from monarchy regarding citizen roles?
Why is the study of democracy focused on democratic politics?
What is the strength and weakness of democracy?

solution_steps.explain: Dictatorships often discourage citizen involvement; democracies require it.
The quality of governance is a reflection of how citizens engage with the system.
Focus on the continuous effort of citizens to strengthen democratic forms.

questions: Which of the following does not lead to the spread of democracy?
What are the difficulties people face in a non-democratic country?
Which freedoms are usually taken away when a democracy is overthrown by the military?
Why was an independent trade union so important in Poland?
How has democracy marched through the twentieth century?
Classify Country A: People who do not accept the country official religion do not have a right to vote.
Classify Country B: The same party has been winning elections for the last twenty years.
Classify Country C: Ruling party has lost in the last three elections.
Classify Country D: There is no independent election commission.
Classify Country P: The parliament cannot pass a law about the army without the consent of the Chief of Army.
Classify Country Q: The parliament cannot pass a law reducing the powers of the judiciary.
Classify Country R: The country leaders cannot sign any treaty with another country without taking permission from its neighbouring country.
Classify Country S: All the major economic decisions about the country are taken by officials of the central bank which the ministers cannot change.
Which of these is not a good argument in favour of democracy? Why?
Identify democratic and undemocratic elements in: A minister said that some laws have to be passed by the parliament in order to conform to the regulations decided by the World Trade Organisation.
Identify democratic and undemocratic elements in: The Election Commission ordered re-polling in a constituency where large scale rigging was reported.
Identify democratic and undemocratic elements in: Women representation in the parliament has never reached 10 per cent. This led women organisations to demand one-third seats for women.
Which of these is not a valid reason for arguing that there is a lesser possibility of famine in a democratic country?
Which of these is not a democratic method for 40 villages to force the government to respond to their need for drinking water?
Write a response to the argument: Army is the most disciplined and corruption-free organisation in the country. Therefore army should rule the country.
Write a response to the argument: Rule of the majority means the rule of ignorant people. What we need is the rule of the wise.
Write a response to the argument: If we want religious leaders to guide us in spiritual matters, why not invite them to guide us in politics as well.
Are the following statements in keeping with democracy as a value? Father to daughter: I don't want to hear your opinion about your marriage.
Are the following statements in keeping with democracy as a value? Teacher to student: Don't disturb my concentration by asking me questions in the classroom.
Are the following statements in keeping with democracy as a value? Employee to the officer: Our working hours must be reduced according to the law.
Decide if a country is a democracy if: All the citizens have right to vote but the government owns the radio and television and newspapers need permission to publish news.
Write an essay on 'Democracy and Poverty' using the information given in the report on USA inequalities.
